```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_smooth, scale_y_log10, scale_x_log10, theme_minimal, labs
from plotnine.data import msleep
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
```

# Introduction to the Mammalian Sleep Dataset

This report describes `msleep`, a data set of 83 mammals, including their body weight, brain size, total hours of sleep, and number of REM cycles.

![Photo by NOAA on Unsplash](images/pilot_whale.jpg)

<!--portion: page --> 

## Sleep by diet

Across all types of diets, there are mammals who spend a substantial portion of their day sleeping.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-top-sleepers
#| tbl-cap: "Top Sleepers"
top_sleepers = (msleep
  .dropna(subset=['vore', 'sleep_total']) 
  .groupby('vore') 
  .apply(lambda x: x.loc[x.sleep_total.idxmax()]) 
  .reset_index(drop=True))

display(top_sleepers)
```

<!--portion: callout --> 

Missing data

```{python}
#| label: missing-data
#| echo: false
n_missing = msleep[['bodywt', 'brainwt', 'sleep_rem']].isna().sum()
```

As you may have noticed above, many values in this data set are missing, so interpret these statistics with caution.
For instance, the variable `sleep_rem` is missing `{python} n_missing['sleep_rem']` values, and `brainwt` is missing `{python} n_missing['brainwt']`, but `bodywt` is missing `{python} n_missing['bodywt']`.

<!--portion: tabset --> 

## REM Cycles by Diet

Another important aspect of sleep is the number of REM cycles.
While number of REM cycles is closely linked to total hours of sleep, the list of top REM cycles by diet is different than above.
Let's take a look at the top REM cyclists by diet.

```{python}
#| label: describe-animal
#| echo: false
top_rem = (msleep.dropna(subset=['vore', 'sleep_rem']) 
  .groupby('vore') 
  .apply(lambda x: x.nlargest(1, 'sleep_rem')) 
  .reset_index(drop=True))

# split into a dictionary of data frames by animal
top_rem_dict = {k: v for k, v in top_rem.groupby('name')}

def describe_animal(animal):
    animal = top_rem_dict[animal]
    return display(Markdown(f"The {animal['name'].iloc[0]} is a {animal['vore'].iloc[0]}vore that weighs {animal['bodywt'].mean()} kilograms on average. It sleeps a total of about {animal['sleep_total'].iloc[0]} hours with {animal['sleep_rem'].iloc[0]} REM cycles."))
```

Giant Armadillo

```{python}
#| label: describe-animal-ga
describe_animal("Giant armadillo")
```

North American Opossum

```{python}
#| label: describe-animal-nao
describe_animal("North American Opossum")
```

Thick-tailed Opossum

```{python}
#| label: describe-animal-tto
describe_animal("Thick-tailed opposum")
```

Thirteen-lined Ground Squirrel

```{python}
#| label: describe-animal-tlgs
describe_animal("Thirteen-lined ground squirrel")
```

<!--portion: columns --> 

## The thirteen-lined ground squirrel's body weight

```{python}
#| label: fig-tlgs-body-wt
#| fig-cap: "The thirteen-lined ground squirrel's body weight among other mammals"
squirrel_data = top_rem_dict["Thirteen-lined ground squirrel"]

(ggplot(msleep, aes(x='sleep_total', y='bodywt')) +
    geom_point(color="#ccc") + 
    geom_point(data=squirrel_data, color="firebrick", size=2.5) + 
    scale_x_log10() + 
    scale_y_log10() + 
    theme_minimal() + 
    labs(x="Total Sleep (hours)", y="Body Weight (kg)"))
```

Thirteen-lined ground squirrels have the most REM cycles among herbivores.
Like a lot of smaller mammals, they sleep a lot.

![[Image source](https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=10724264)](images/Chomp_2.jpg)

<!--portion: ncol --> 

## Body weight, brain size, and sleep

Mammals who sleep longer have smaller bodies and brains.

```{python}
#| label: fig-sleep-total
#| fig-cap: 
#|   - "Sleep total versus body weight"
#|   - "Sleep total versus brain weight"
p1 = (ggplot(msleep, aes('sleep_total', 'bodywt')) + 
  geom_point(color="#ccc") + 
  geom_smooth(color="#4682B4") + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  scale_x_log10() + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs(x="Total Sleep (hours)", y="Body Weight (kg)"))

p2 = (ggplot(msleep, aes('sleep_total', 'brainwt')) + 
  geom_point(color="#ccc") + 
  geom_smooth(color="#4682B4") + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  scale_x_log10() + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs(x="Total Sleep (hours)", y="Brain Weight (kg)"))
  
p1, p2
```

<!--portion: margins --> 

## Revisiting the top REM cyclists

```{python}
#| label: tbl-top-rem
#| tbl-cap: "Top REM Cycles by Diet"
display(top_rem[['name', 'vore', 'sleep_total', 'sleep_rem']])
```

The North American Opossum is the omnivore with the highest number of REM cycles as well as the longest average sleep time.

![[Image source](https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=11491)](images/Opossum-drawing.jpg)

<!--portion: codemargins --> 

## Considering sleep total vs. REM cycles

Unsurprisingly, sleep total is closely linked to REM cycles, but it's not the only factor.
Two mammals, the North American opossum and the thick-tailed opossum are the top sleepers and REM cyclists for their diets.
The little brown bat, while the top sleeper among insectivores, has a meager 2 REM cycles on average.
Notably, the Arctic ground squirrel is missing data on number of REM cycles.

```{python}
#| label: top-sleepers
#| fig-cap: "Sleep Total vs. REM Cycles"
#| tbl-cap: "Top Sleepers"
p3 = (ggplot(msleep, aes(x='sleep_total', y='sleep_rem')) + 
    geom_point(color='#ccc') + 
    geom_point(data=top_sleepers, color='firebrick', size=2.5) + 
    scale_x_log10() + 
    scale_y_log10() + 
    theme_minimal() + 
    labs(x='Total Sleep (hours)', y='Number of REM cycles'))

t1 = display(top_sleepers[['name', 'vore', 'sleep_total', 'sleep_rem']])

p3, t1
```
